_meta.note: L1/L2 support tickets only. L3 engineering escalations tracked separately in Jira (SUPP-* project). Ticket volume reflects enterprise and mid-market accounts only — SMB self-serve tickets excluded unless escalated.

levels.L1: How-to, configuration, billing questions — frontline support resolves within 1-2 days
levels.L2: Technical issues requiring specialist — 3-5 day SLA, may escalate to L3
levels.escalation_to_L3: When engineering fix required — L2 creates Jira ticket, becomes L3

summary.volume_trend: L2 volume peaked Mar-May on NovaAI reliability, fell sharply after DR-006, then produced a sharp one-week spike in early July from GA load (INC-2026-0121) before dropping again once the circuit breaker shipped Jul 31. August L2 volume is the lowest of the year. L1 v1-migration questions fell as mid-market migration reached 96%, but the residual tail is now concentrated: the last 8 customers generate disproportionate ticket volume because v1 capacity was scaled down around them. Mobile ticket volume rose from Jul 31 with soft GA, as expected for a launch.
summary.periodNote: Jul 1 - Aug 10 added 42 tickets (8 shown here as program-relevant). The window's most consequential ticket is SC-2026-0399: an enterprise CDO asking a direct question about the SOC 2 date, arriving through support rather than through the account team.

pattern1.name: NovaAI reliability / model serving errors
pattern1.description: High volume of L2 tickets for model serving timeouts, inference errors, and unexpected HTTP 5xx. Correlates with INC-2026-0034, 0052, 0078, 0089. Declined sharply after DR-006 connection pool fix (Jun 10 onward: 2 L2 tickets vs. 23 in prior 3 months).
pattern1.programRelevance: ATLAS — uptime problem (94.2% baseline). Root cause identified, DR-006 improvement plan in effect.
pattern1.updateNote: Pattern re-activated Jul 6-31 under GA load, then closed out. Three tickets in the window vs 23 across Mar-May. Proactive disclosure by Marcus Chen on the day of the incident is why none of the three became an account escalation.

pattern2.name: v1 API deprecation confusion / migration questions
pattern2.description: High and growing volume of tickets about v1 API end-of-life timeline, SDK migration questions, and v1 API bugs. L1: 'When is v1 going away?' L2: 'Our v1 integration is breaking, please help migrate.' Peak in Apr-May as deprecation communications began. Supports MERIDIAN migration urgency.
pattern2.programRelevance: MERIDIAN — migration velocity. SMB Compass partner engagement directly reduces ticket volume expected from Aug.
pattern2.updateNote: Declining but concentrating. Mid-market reached 96% and SMB 94%, so absolute volume is down - but the remaining 8 mid-market customers now generate a disproportionate share, and SC-2026-0409 shows the v1 infrastructure being scaled down faster than the customers are actually leaving it.

pattern3.name: Pipeline reliability (Airflow instability)
pattern3.description: L2 tickets from FlowEngine customers experiencing pipeline delays, missed schedules, and data freshness issues. Correlates with INC-2026-0039, 0055, 0094. Airflow scheduler instability is the primary root cause. Customers explicitly asking about migration timeline.
affectedAccounts: 8 enterprise customers with pipeline SLA dependencies
pattern3.programRelevance: PULSE — Airflow→Temporal migration urgency. L2 ticket volume is supporting evidence for M4 prioritization.
pattern3.updateNote: Effectively closed. FlowEngine migration completed Aug 7; pipeline success rate is 99.6% in August, above target for the first time this year. Expect this pattern to disappear once Airflow is decommissioned.

pattern4.name: SOC 2 / compliance documentation requests
pattern4.description: Enterprise prospects and pilot customers requesting SOC 2 evidence documentation, security questionnaires, and compliance attestations. Volume increasing as pipeline grows (ATLAS GA approach). Financial services and healthcare accounts generate the most requests.
pattern4.programRelevance: SHIELD — SOC 2 certification. These tickets are converting to blocked deals. M3 close May 26 addressed immediate requests.
pattern4.updateNote: Changed in character, not volume. Requests are no longer 'do you have SOC 2 evidence' - 100 controls are complete and evidenced. They are now 'what exactly will you have, and when'. SC-2026-0399 is the template: customers are tracking the Dec 15 report date, and answering that precisely now matters more than control counts.

pattern5.name: Mobile alpha feedback (internal + Kestrel)
pattern5.description: L1 feedback tickets from internal HORIZON alpha testers and early Kestrel preview users. Topics: iOS alert center UX, Android notification reliability, offline sync behavior. Being tracked in dedicated HORIZON feedback channel — not traditional support. Priya Kaur receiving and triaging.
pattern5.programRelevance: HORIZON — beta cohort quality. Low severity, high signal value for pre-beta polish.
pattern5.updateNote: Volume up from beta (Jul 2) and soft GA (Jul 31) as expected. Mix shifted from alpha UX nitpicks to real integration issues (SC-2026-0402) and forward-looking feature requests (SC-2026-0405) - a healthier signal than the alpha-period feedback.

tickets.subject: NovaAI inference API returning 502 errors — production model calls failing
tickets.summary: Apex Health production integration returning HTTP 502 errors on NovaAI inference calls during their morning ETL window (07:00-09:00 PT). Approximately 34% of inference requests failing. Patient risk-stratification pipeline downstream is blocked. Derek confirmed they are retrying on 503 but not 502 — correct retry logic not triggering.
tickets.resolution: L2 confirmed wrong HTTP status code returned by NovaAI API on capacity overload (502 instead of 503). Immediate workaround: Derek updated client to retry on both 502 and 503. Escalated to L3 (SUPP-2026-0034) for permanent fix. L3 fix deployed Sprint 12 — 502/503 correction live. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: ATLAS — confirmed contribution to 94.2% uptime baseline. Root cause fixed in SUPP-2026-0034.

tickets.subject: NovaAI model serving timeouts — inference p99 latency exceeding 45 seconds
tickets.summary: Nuvera Insurance reporting p99 inference latency spiking to 45+ seconds during business hours. Underwriting model calls backing up — analysts waiting on predictions. SLA commitment to internal business unit (30-second max) at risk. Ananya confirmed issue is intermittent, correlates with concurrent request volume above ~150 req/min.
tickets.resolution: L2 identified connection pool exhaustion under concurrent enterprise load — same root cause as INC-2026-0034. Workaround: Nuvera temporarily reduced concurrent request rate to 80 req/min via their batch scheduler. Permanent fix addressed in SUPP-2026-0018 (connection pool limit increase + jitter). Full resolution deployed Apr 15. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: ATLAS — uptime degradation. Connected to connection pool root cause (SUPP-2026-0018).

tickets.subject: NovaAI API intermittent 500 errors — hot-reload cycle after model update
tickets.summary: VantagePoint experiencing 500 errors for approximately 8-12 minutes following each NovaAI model hot-reload event. Three model updates per week on average — causing recurring production disruption. Tomasz identified the pattern: errors begin immediately after model update notification and persist until next request succeeds. Suspect dangling tensor references in reload sequence.
tickets.resolution: L2 reproduced the issue in staging. Confirmed memory leak after hot-reload — dangling tensor references not cleaned up. Escalated to L3 (SUPP-2026-0078) for engineering fix. Fix merged in hot-patch release Apr 6 (explicit tensor cleanup in reload sequence). VantagePoint confirmed resolution Apr 8. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: ATLAS — model serving stability. Also relevant to SPARK (same model serving infrastructure).

tickets.subject: NovaAI inference 502 errors — enterprise beta account reporting full outage
tickets.summary: Marcus Webb (CISO, escalating on behalf of engineering team) reported full NovaAI service unavailability during a scheduled POC demo window. POC kickoff call had to be rescheduled. This is a deal-sensitive incident — Marcus is the CISO evaluating whether to proceed with the enterprise contract. Ticket flagged as deal-risk by AE Priya Shah.
tickets.resolution: L2 confirmed INC-2026-0052 was active — connection pool exhaustion under concurrent load. Immediate mitigation: enterprise beta pool isolated from shared pool within 40 minutes. Marcus Webb briefed by Priya Shah within 1 hour. POC demo rescheduled for Apr 7 — completed successfully. Permanent fix in SUPP-2026-0018. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: ATLAS — deal-sensitive incident. Apex Health POC outcome (CLOSED WON Jun 16) demonstrates recovery.

tickets.subject: NovaAI inference capacity — post-GA load causing latency regression
tickets.summary: Finex Capital (signed Jun 22, 2 days prior) reporting elevated inference latency post-GA. p95 latency at 12 seconds vs. 3-second baseline from POC. Alicia Monroe submitted directly — high urgency given just signed contract. Volume increase post-ATLAS GA may be causing capacity pressure. L2 investigating whether this is isolated or portfolio-wide.
tickets.resolution: Open. L2 investigating. Preliminary finding: post-ATLAS GA concurrent request volume increased 3.4x from POC baselines. Capacity scaling triggered. Expected resolution within 24 hours via auto-scaling config update. Alicia Monroe updated via email Jun 25.
tickets.programRelevance: ATLAS — post-GA capacity management. New customer onboarding scenario.

tickets.subject: v1 API end-of-life date — when will v1 be shut down?
tickets.summary: Sophie Andersson asking for official v1 API end-of-life date. Internal planning question — Thornbridge renewal decision depends on migration timeline certainty. Sophie needs a committed date to plan her engineering team's Q2 workload.
tickets.resolution: L1 confirmed v1 API support guaranteed through Sep 30 2026. Directed Sophie to MERIDIAN M1 migration guide and Python SDK v2 documentation. Noted that dedicated migration tooling will be available Apr 2026. Sophie acknowledged — satisfied with response.
tickets.programRelevance: MERIDIAN — v1 EoL communications. Thornbridge subsequently migrated Jun 2026 (MERIDIAN M5).

tickets.subject: Python SDK v2 migration guide — how to migrate from v1 requests to v2 client?
tickets.summary: Developer asking for migration guide from v1 REST calls to Python SDK v2. Specific question: how to handle pagination changes between v1 and v2. Also asking whether v1 API keys will work with v2 SDK (they will, with migration step). Typical SMB migration question.
tickets.resolution: L1 directed to docs.novagrid.io/sdk-v2/migration. Confirmed v1 API keys continue to work during transition period. Sent code snippet for pagination migration pattern. Ryan confirmed resolved.
tickets.programRelevance: MERIDIAN — migration volume indicator. 67 similar L1 tickets filed Jan-Jun 2026.

tickets.subject: v1 API rate limiter returning 429 with no Retry-After header — client backoff broken
tickets.summary: Nuvera Insurance integration receiving 429 Too Many Requests from v1 API but with no Retry-After header in the response. Their client-side backoff logic depends on Retry-After — without it, they default to a fixed 1-second retry which is causing a retry storm and amplifying the rate limit problem. Ananya confirmed this behavior is consistent across all enterprise endpoints.
tickets.resolution: L2 confirmed bug: v1 API rate limiter omitting Retry-After header on all 429 responses — affects all API consumers. Escalated to L3 (SUPP-2026-0052). Workaround provided: implement exponential backoff with jitter, starting at 2 seconds. Permanent fix deployed in Sprint 13 — Retry-After header now included on all 429s. Nuvera confirmed resolution Apr 22. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: MERIDIAN — v1 API quality. Also affects migration urgency: v1 bugs are compounding migration motivation.

tickets.subject: v1 API deprecation announcement — email received, confused about Sep 30 vs Dec 31 dates
tickets.summary: Naomi Park received deprecation notice email and is confused about two dates mentioned: 'Sep 30 support degradation' and 'Dec 31 full shutdown.' Asking which date she needs to plan to. Also asking whether her current v1 integration will 'just stop working' or if there will be a grace period.
tickets.resolution: L1 clarified: Sep 30 2026 is the date when v1 API enters reduced support (no new features, critical security patches only). Dec 31 2026 is the full EoL date. Integrations will return 410 Gone after Dec 31. Directed Naomi to migration guide. Offered Compass partner migration session (free for SMB). Naomi acknowledged.
tickets.programRelevance: MERIDIAN — SMB communication effectiveness. Pattern 2 ticket confirming documentation clarity gap.

tickets.subject: FlowEngine DAG missed scheduled runs — pipeline delayed 6+ hours
tickets.summary: ClearPath Analytics FlowEngine pipeline missed 3 consecutive scheduled runs. DAGs were queued but not executing — Airflow scheduler showed tasks in 'queued' state for 6+ hours. Downstream data delivery to ClearPath's client reports delayed. SLA breach — ClearPath flagged this as a contractual issue.
tickets.resolution: L2 confirmed Airflow scheduler memory leak — scheduler process had been running for 14 days, memory usage at 94% of container limit. Restarted scheduler process — DAGs executed immediately. Workaround deployed: nightly scheduler restart scheduled via cron. Full fix deferred to PULSE M4 (Temporal migration). ClearPath offered SLA credit. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: PULSE — Airflow instability. Nightly restart workaround reduces symptoms. Root fix in PULSE M4.

tickets.subject: FlowEngine pipeline data freshness SLA breach — customer reporting 4-hour lag
tickets.summary: Glenmore Capital pipeline showing 4-hour data freshness lag vs. 30-minute SLA. Lucia confirmed the lag appeared gradually over 3 days — not a single event. Glenmore's risk models depend on fresh data — internal downstream processes blocked. Lucia explicitly asked whether NovaGrid is 'planning to replace Airflow' — direct migration readiness question.
tickets.resolution: L2 identified Airflow DAG scheduler memory leak (SUPP-2026-0041 root cause) compounded by Glenmore's large DAG count (847 tasks). Nightly scheduler restart workaround applied. L2 briefed Lucia on Temporal migration roadmap (PULSE M4 target Jun 2026 — now Jun 10 completed). Data freshness restored within 2 hours of restart. Ticket closed Apr 19.
tickets.programRelevance: PULSE — Airflow instability. Enterprise account asking directly about Temporal migration. PULSE M5 close (Jun 10) resolves root cause.

tickets.subject: Airflow/Temporal mixed environment — NovaAI pipeline scheduling conflict
tickets.summary: Glenmore Capital migrated 60% of their pipelines to Temporal (pilot migration program) but remaining Airflow DAGs are conflicting with Temporal workers for NovaAI pipeline scheduling. NovaAI inference pipelines running on shared Temporal worker pool are being starved by Airflow task queuing. Lucia confirmed the contention started exactly when Temporal was introduced.
tickets.resolution: L2 diagnosed resource contention between Airflow and Temporal workers on shared NovaAI pipeline infrastructure. Workaround: dedicated Temporal worker pool provisioned for NovaAI pipelines — isolated from shared pool. Full resolution in SUPP-2026-0095 (PULSE M5 close Jun 10). Lucia confirmed stable operation May 12. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: PULSE — Airflow-to-Temporal migration overlap period. SUPP-2026-0095 engineering ticket tracks full resolution.

tickets.subject: SOC 2 evidence package request — Meridian Financial legal team requirement
tickets.summary: Yvonne Tran formally requesting SOC 2 Type II evidence documentation for Meridian Financial legal due diligence. Legal team has 90-day clause — SOC 2 evidence must be in progress or completed by May 1 2026. Yvonne needs: current control completion count, Deloitte engagement letter, and estimated certification date. Flagged as deal-blocking by AE Dmitri Volkov.
tickets.resolution: L2 escalated to SHIELD team (Marcus Chen). Provided in-progress SOC 2 status update: 22 controls completed, Deloitte engaged, target date Aug 2026. Yvonne acknowledged and shared with legal team. Deal continued in pipeline. Meridian Financial legal 90-day clause satisfied by SHIELD M3 close May 26 (evidence package submitted May 12).
tickets.programRelevance: SHIELD — SOC 2 certification. Blocked deal converted to active pipeline following evidence package delivery.

tickets.subject: SOC 2 security questionnaire — Apex Health POC approval requirement
tickets.summary: Marcus Webb (CISO) submitted a 47-question enterprise security questionnaire as a pre-condition for POC approval. Questions cover: data encryption at rest and in transit, access control model (RBAC/ABAC), incident response SLAs, data residency, HIPAA controls documentation, and SOC 2 roadmap. Marcus indicated POC will not proceed without satisfactory responses to all 47 questions.
tickets.resolution: L2 routed to SHIELD compliance team (Marcus Chen) and ATLAS engineering lead (Jamie Chen). Response package prepared over 12 business days: 47/47 questions answered, HIPAA controls documentation (in-progress version) attached, encryption architecture diagram provided. Marcus Webb reviewed — approved POC May 5. Ticket closed Mar 4 (initial response); POC approval confirmed separately.
tickets.programRelevance: SHIELD + ATLAS — compliance as a sales gate. Apex Health CLOSED WON Jun 16 ($360K initial) — this questionnaire was a critical milestone.

tickets.subject: Nuvera Insurance SOC 2 progress update request — CDO board deadline
tickets.summary: Rajiv Patel submitted formal SOC 2 progress update request — has a Q3 board meeting where he must present vendor compliance posture for all data platform vendors. Rajiv asked specifically for: (1) current control count, (2) Deloitte audit engagement confirmation, (3) expected Type II certification date, and (4) what happens if certification slips past Aug 2026. Flagged as board-level deadline by AE Sarah James.
tickets.resolution: L2 escalated to Marcus Chen (SHIELD PM). Response provided Mar 12: 48 controls completed (out of 86 in scope), Deloitte engagement letter attached, Aug 2026 certification target confirmed, and contingency briefing (interim Type I-equivalent evidence package available if Type II slips). Rajiv acknowledged — satisfied with progress trajectory. Relationship maintained.
tickets.programRelevance: SHIELD — SOC 2 certification. CDO board deadline (Q3) aligns with Aug 2026 target. Nuvera probability now 80%.

tickets.subject: Corinthia Bank — GDPR data residency and EU hosting documentation request
tickets.summary: Henrik Svensson (CTO, Corinthia Bank — in final contracting) submitted formal documentation request for GDPR Article 28 compliance evidence and EU data residency architecture documentation. Corinthia Bank is EMEA-headquartered with Swedish banking license — GDPR data residency is a legal requirement for production use. Kai Müller (AE) flagged this as deal-blocking if not addressed in contracting.
tickets.resolution: Open. L2 routed to SHIELD (Marcus Chen) and Legal (Priya Kumar). Response in progress. Current position: NovaGrid processes data in US-East and EU-West regions; EU-West hosting can be configured for Corinthia Bank's production tenant. Full GDPR data residency guarantee (no data leaving EU) requires EU data residency initiative (company-level, Q1 2027 roadmap). AE Kai Müller to caveat in contracting language. Response due Jun 28.
tickets.programRelevance: SHIELD + ATLAS — compliance documentation. Active deal in final contracting (OPP-2026-228, $200K initial, $3.1M potential).

tickets.subject: HORIZON alpha — iOS alert center dismissal not persisting across app restart
tickets.summary: Internal alpha tester reporting that dismissed alerts in the iOS alert center reappear after app restart. Expected behavior: dismissed alerts should persist as dismissed. Actual behavior: all alerts re-show as unread after cold app restart. Affects daily-use experience for alert-heavy users.
tickets.resolution: L1 acknowledged and routed to HORIZON engineering (Priya Kaur). Root cause: alert dismiss state stored only in memory, not in local SQLite store. Fix: persist dismiss state to local DB on dismiss action. Fix deployed in alpha build 1.4.2 (May 19). David confirmed resolved.
tickets.programRelevance: HORIZON — beta cohort polish. Alert persistence is a core UX requirement for the alert center feature.

tickets.subject: HORIZON alpha — Android push notifications not arriving when app in background
tickets.summary: Nina Ross (AE, internal tester) reporting that Android push notifications do not arrive when the app is backgrounded. iOS push is working correctly. Android background notification delivery appears to depend on whether Google Play Services FCM is active — some test devices with battery optimization enabled are blocking FCM delivery.
tickets.resolution: L1 routed to HORIZON engineering (Priya Kaur). Root cause: FCM high-priority flag not set — Android treats as low-priority and defers delivery under battery optimization. Fix: set FCM priority to 'high' for real-time alert notifications. Deployed alpha build 1.5.1 (Jun 3). Nina confirmed resolved on both test devices.
tickets.programRelevance: HORIZON — beta cohort quality. FCM priority fix is a pre-requisite for reliable push notification delivery in beta.

tickets.subject: HORIZON mobile alpha — Kestrel preview offline sync dropping writes
tickets.summary: Luca Ferraro (Kestrel preview access) reporting that notes written in offline mode are being dropped when the app reconnects to the network. Expected: offline writes sync to server on reconnect. Actual: offline queue cleared without sync on connectivity restoration. Luca flagged this as a blocking issue for Kestrel's editorial workflow use case — field reporters often work in low-connectivity environments.
tickets.resolution: L1 escalated priority (deal-sensitive account) and routed to HORIZON engineering. Root cause: offline write queue flush executed before network handshake confirmed — race condition on reconnect. Fix: implement queue flush only after successful network ping-ack. Deployed alpha build 1.6.0 (Jun 18). Luca confirmed resolved and 'much more confident in the offline story now.' AE Nina Ross briefed.
tickets.programRelevance: HORIZON — beta quality. Offline sync reliability is a key differentiator for Kestrel's use case. Fix directly supports beta readiness.

tickets.subject: Auth service returning 401 on valid tokens — enterprise auth regression
tickets.summary: Elena Markov (CTO) reporting that VantagePoint's production integration started returning 401 Unauthorized on API calls that were working the day before. API tokens confirmed valid — token expiry not the issue. Elena confirmed the behavior started at approximately 14:30 PST Feb 23 — correlates with a NovaGrid infrastructure change window. Entire VantagePoint production pipeline blocked.
tickets.resolution: L2 identified Auth0 token refresh storm pattern — connection pool for Auth service exhausted during a concurrent enterprise onboarding event the same afternoon. VantagePoint tokens were technically valid but auth service was returning 401 due to connection pool exhaustion misrouting. Workaround: auth service restart restored service within 22 minutes. Escalated to L3 (SUPP-2026-0018) for permanent fix. Elena briefed by Dmitri Volkov. Ticket closed Mar 2.
tickets.programRelevance: ATLAS — auth service stability. Connection pool root cause confirmed. SUPP-2026-0018 fix (jitter + pool increase) deployed Apr 15.

tickets.subject: SAML 2.0 SSO configuration — Nuvera Insurance cannot use OIDC
tickets.summary: Nuvera Insurance corporate SSO is SAML 2.0 (Ping Identity) — their IT policy prohibits OIDC-based SSO for regulated data platforms. Ananya requesting confirmation that NovaAI Enterprise supports SAML 2.0. ATLAS SSO feature set was at M3 (just closed Apr 25) — L2 needed to verify SAML support scope.
tickets.resolution: L2 confirmed ATLAS M3 (SAML/OIDC SSO) includes SAML 2.0 support. Identified issue: Ananya's configuration error — entity ID mismatch between Nuvera's Ping Identity setup and NovaGrid SAML SP metadata. L2 walked Ananya through configuration correction. SAML SSO confirmed working Mar 11. Ticket closed. Escalated to L3 feature request (SUPP-2026-0103) for documentation improvement.
tickets.programRelevance: ATLAS — M3 SSO delivery. SAML support confirmed. Configuration documentation gap identified.

tickets.subject: DataCore query engine — p99 latency spike on dashboard reports post v2.3.1 deploy
tickets.summary: VantagePoint Analytics reporting p99 dashboard report generation latency spiked from ~4 seconds to 28 seconds following NovaGrid DataCore v2.3.1 deploy. Complex scan queries (joining 3+ tables with window functions) are disproportionately affected. Tomasz confirmed the regression appeared exactly after the v2.3.1 deploy window on May 7.
tickets.resolution: L2 confirmed query optimizer regression introduced in v2.3.1 — hot path rewrite had unintended side effect on complex scan plans. DataCore v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.3.0 within 4 hours of ticket submission. Fix delivered in v2.3.2 (query optimizer hot path rewrite corrected). Tomasz confirmed p99 latency returned to ~4 seconds after v2.3.2 deploy May 14. Ticket closed May 15.
tickets.programRelevance: NEXUS — DataCore service quality. Performance regression in a named release. SUPP-2026-0067 tracks engineering fix.

tickets.subject: Billing — how to add a second payment method for enterprise contract split invoicing
tickets.summary: Sophie Andersson asking how to configure split invoicing — Thornbridge has two cost centers (Trading Tech and Risk Platform) that need separate invoices for the same NovaGrid contract. Asking if this is configurable in the billing portal or requires manual RevOps intervention.
tickets.resolution: L1 confirmed split invoicing requires RevOps configuration — not self-serve in billing portal. Routed Sophie to kai.muller@novagrid.io (AE) who coordinated with RevOps. Split invoicing configured within 2 business days. Sophie confirmed.
tickets.programRelevance: None direct. MERIDIAN context: Thornbridge migration progress (renewal now confirmed) makes billing questions an indicator of healthy customer relationship.

tickets.subject: Mobile session token expiry — iOS users being logged out unexpectedly
tickets.summary: Priya Kaur reporting that internal iOS alpha testers are being logged out unexpectedly — approximately 15% of alpha users experiencing session termination within 2-4 hours of app use with background refresh active. Token expiry window appears too aggressive for background refresh patterns. Escalated from INC-2026-0098. Affects user experience testing validity — testers who get logged out are submitting negative feedback that may not reflect final product behavior.
tickets.resolution: L2 confirmed: session token TTL set to 2 hours for alpha builds (security default). Background refresh pattern — where the app checks for updates every 15 minutes — was consuming token lifetime faster than expected. Config change: session token TTL extended to 24 hours for alpha/beta builds; production will use 8 hours with silent refresh. Deployed Jun 1. Priya confirmed logout rate dropped to <1% of alpha sessions. Ticket closed.
tickets.programRelevance: HORIZON — alpha quality. Session token TTL config deployed. Escalated from INC-2026-0098 (SUPP-2026-0118 tracks engineering config).

tickets.subject: Slow dashboard loads and session refresh delays after platform auth change
tickets.summary: Derek reported dashboard loads taking 4-6 seconds from around 09:00 UTC. Correlated to the NEXUS IAM token refresh latency incident (INC-2026-0117). Resolved same day by the platform fix; Derek confirmed normal performance by EOD.

tickets.subject: Intermittent 5xx errors on NovaAI inference calls - production impact
tickets.summary: Roughly 2% of inference requests returning 5xx during the Jul 6 GA-load event. Patient risk-stratification pipeline degraded but not blocked. Marcus Chen contacted Derek proactively the same afternoon rather than waiting for the ticket to escalate - Derek noted this explicitly in his response and it is the reason this stayed a P1 ticket rather than an account escalation. Held open until the circuit breaker shipped Jul 31.

tickets.subject: Inference latency and occasional errors during morning batch window
tickets.summary: Same underlying cause as SC-2026-0391. Alicia was briefed on the capacity response and the Jul 31 circuit breaker date, and accepted the timeline.

tickets.subject: When will our tenant provisioning complete? Onboarding appears paused
tickets.summary: Henrik noticed provisioning had stalled after signature. Kai Muller and Marcus Chen explained the DR-011 onboarding rate limit directly - new tenants were deliberately held while platform uptime sat below the internal floor. Henrik's response was that he would rather be told than discover it. Provisioning resumed Aug 3.

tickets.subject: SOC 2 certification date - our board pack says August, is that confirmed?
tickets.summary: Rajiv asked directly whether SOC 2 Type II certification would be in hand on Aug 31. Answered honestly per DR-014: Aug 31 is audit-readiness, the Type II report is Dec 15. Rajiv's Q3 board window cannot be met, and the opportunity moved to Q4. The single clearest commercial cost of the date restatement - and it arrived as a support ticket, not through the account team.

tickets.subject: Beta users being logged out of the mobile app unexpectedly
tickets.summary: Roughly 60 beta users across Kestrel and Solaris logged out mid-session as the first cohort crossed the 24-hour token boundary, three days after soft GA. Fixed within 92 minutes.

tickets.subject: Mobile app feedback - offline mode and alert filtering
tickets.summary: Feature feedback rather than a defect. Tom's team wants offline read access and saved alert filters. Logged for HORIZON post-GA backlog. Notable as a signal: Solaris is engaging with the product rather than the schedule for the first time since the DR-008 expectation gap.

tickets.subject: v1 API batch jobs running slow during nightly window
tickets.summary: Three of the eight remaining v1 mid-market customers reporting slow batch runs. Cause is v1 gateway capacity having been scaled down on a migration curve that assumed these customers would be gone by Aug 1. Gateway scaled back up; stays open until MERIDIAN M6 closes.
